## Natural history notes

A tiny delphacid planthopper characterized by a narrow wedge-shaped body, delicate roof-held wings, and pale yellowish to brownish coloration typical of grass-associated planthoppers. In Florida, Flavoclypeus andromedus is recorded from the state and has been collected from natural areas; it has also been noted from several grass hosts, so it is most likely encountered in grassy wetlands, wet prairies, pine flatwoods, roadsides, fields, and other low vegetation. Adults and nymphs feed by piercing grasses or related plants and drinking sap, while serving as prey for spiders, predatory bugs, small wasps, and other insect predators.
